disease_name: Hypercholesterolaemia, Mixed dyslipidaemia, Cardiovascular disease, Hyperlipidemia following transplantation
indication: Treatment of primary (familial) hypercholesterolaemia or mixed dyslipidaemia, Reduction of mortality and the frequency of cardiovascular disease in patients with moderate to severe hypercholesterolemia and at high risk of a first cardiovascular event, Reduction of hyperlipidemia following transplantation
mechanism_of_action: blocking of an enzyme important in the synthesis of cholesterol, called HMG-CoA reductase
side_effects: muscle problems such as myalgia, myopathy, rhabdomyolysis (even fatal)
unsuitable_population: patients with active liver disease, marked and lasting increase in levels of transaminases in the blood, kidney failure, hypothyroidism, muscle toxicity from statins and fibrates or another cholesterol-lowering medicine, hereditary muscle disorders, alcoholism, over 70 years old

indication: treatment of primary hypercholesterolaemia or mixed dyslipidemia, reduction of cardiovascular mortality and morbidity in patients with moderate to severe hypercholesterolaemia and at high risk of a first cardiovascular event, reduction of post-transplant hyperlipidaemia in patients undergoing immunosuppressive therapy following solid organ transplantation
recommended_usage: swallowed with water || take without food
single_dose: adults 10 mg - 40 mg, children not recommended, elderly no special condition, patients with moderate or severe renal impairment or significant hepatic impairment 10 mg per day
mechanism_of_action: reduces cholesterol levels by inhibiting HMG-CoA reductase enzyme in the liver
side_effects: muscle weakness, interstitial lung disease, diabetes mellitus, dermatomyositis, hepatotoxicity, myalgia, myopathy, rhabdomyolysis
unsuitable_population: children under 18 years, patients with active liver disease or alcoholism, patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, patients with elevated HDL cholesterol
